statement.p: Use Green's Theorem to evaluate the line integral \oint_{\mathcal{C}} y^{8}\,dx + x^{4}\,dy
where \mathcal{C} is the boundary of the square -1\le x \le 1, -1\le y \le 1 oriented counterclockwise.

static.solution:
We have P= y^{8} and Q= x^{4}, therefore \frac{\partial Q}{\partial x}-\frac{\partial P}{\partial y}=4x^{3}-8y^{7} Using Green's Theorem we obtain \int_{\mathcal{C}} y^{8} \,dx+ x^{4} \,dy = \iint_{\mathcal{D}}\left( \frac{\partial Q}{\partial x}-\frac{\partial P}{\partial y} \right) \,dA= \iint_{\mathcal{D}} (4x^{3}-8y^{7}) \,dx \,dy =4\iint_{\mathcal{D}} x^{3} \,dx \,dy-8\iint_{\mathcal{D}} y^{7} \,dx \,dy By symmetry, the positive and negative values of x cancel each other in the first integral, so this integral is zero.
The second double integral is zero by similar reasoning. Therefore, \int_{\mathcal{C}} y^{8} \,dx+ x^{4} \,dy=0-0=0
